newsitem.title: CHINA: China says natural market forces cooled bourses.
newsitem.headline: China says natural market forces cooled bourses.

text.p: China's stock markets, which soared more than 50 percent before recent corrections, had been brought under control by natural market forces, rather than administrative edicts, the Financial News said on Thursday.

Regulations introduced since May, which have seen the bourses in Shanghai and Shenzhen lose around 30 percent of their value, had been aimed at protecting the interests of ordinary investors, the newspaper, mouthpiece of China's central bank, said.

"In the past two months, relevant departments under the State Council (the cabinet), have taken a series of measures to regulate the stock markets to curb a new round of excessive speculation," the newspaper said.

"But a few investors have misunderstood the measures as administrative edicts, and have said that the correction resulting from natural market forces was the result of government intervention to depress the share indices," it said.
A new round of excessive speculation had seen Shanghai's composite index surge 36 percent between March 12 and May 12 and its Shenzhen counterpart by 56 percent, the newspaper said.
"With a price-earnings ratio of 50 to 60 times, the stock market trend veered in a direction seriously incompatible with the national economy," it said.
All these factors indicated that the markets needed a correction and the government only reacted in accordance with that need, the newspaper said.
In addition, the central government had resorted to market means and laws to regulate the markets instead of using administrative edicts, it said.
The government had raised stamp tax for stock trading to 0.5 percent from 0.3 percent and had allowed more new share issues to cool down demand, it said.
It had re-affirmed a ban on state bank money flowing into the stock markets in accordance with relevant laws, it said.
"All these measures are not administrative inteference, let alone government efforts to depress the stock markets," the newspaper said.
Overheating of the stock markets had partially been checked after the recent measures but problems still existed, including excessive speculation, it said.
"If there are no rulers and compasses, you cannot make squares and circles," the newspaper said. "Standardisation will be a long-term task for the stock markets."
